notes: Four running states: lowest first cost, best gain after one deal, lowest second cost net of that gain, best gain after two. Splitting the journey at every town and scanning both sides again is right and far over budget. Taking the two biggest unbroken climbs misses two climbs that should join across a dip; adding every rise forgets there are only two deals.

traps: one long climb is worth splitting at a dip inside it
three climbs: two of them join across a small dip
a single climb needs only one deal
scanning both sides again for every town is over budget

rejects.name: tries every town between the two deals and scans both sides again
takes the two biggest unbroken climbs
adds up every rise, as if deals were unlimited
